source_scope: Original 1647 PDF324 below divider through PDF330 above next divider; printed290–296
source_table_handling: Printed image primary; 30x16 longitude step reconstruction separate and explicitly editorial

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Chapter XLVII begins below the horizontal divider as Of the CRYSIS in Diseases.
preconditions: Printed heading below the conclusion of XLVI.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Separate title-boundary unit; not a patient or a calculated event.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The chapter opens by calling a crisis a 'duell or contention betwixt nature and the infirmity'; it is a good crisis when nature overcomes the disease's malignity.
preconditions: The alleged contest between nature and illness has nature prevailing.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is the historical metaphor, not an independently observed outcome.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Lilly calls the crisis harmful when the sickness prevails.
preconditions: The disease prevails in the alleged contest.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not a numerical or independent prognosis.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: A crisis is described as a sudden bodily alteration during sickness tending either to recovery or further disease.
preconditions: Sick person and sudden change.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not collapse it into guaranteed cure or death; an unfavourable crisis can mean further sickness.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Critical, decretory and chrysmal days are stated to be 'all one', yielding a 'certaine and more sure judgment' about whether the infirmity afflicts more powerfully or less at the true crisis.
preconditions: Conditioned on the actual crisis and how strongly the infirmity afflicts.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The phrase more/less modifies the disease's affliction, not the observer's degree of certainty.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The preferred anchor for a true crisis is the moment when the illness first began.
preconditions: An actual onset moment is known.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Requires timing the Moon to the exact onset, not asking date or patient birth data.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: If illness onset cannot be obtained, Lilly substitutes the very hour when the urine sample was first brought to the doctor for advice.
preconditions: Onset missing AND specimen first-delivery moment known.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Explicitly said to be less certain than onset; not a clinical diagnostic recommendation.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: If no urine is presented, the fallback is the doctor's first conversation when the patient asks for judgment and advice.
preconditions: No urine, doctor and patient first speak, and the sick person seeks an opinion.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not interchange this with any generic doctor visit or retroactively insert consent from other aphorisms.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Lilly attributes to Galen the view that every sudden and vehement motion of disease may be termed a crisis.
preconditions: Attributed ancient-author definition.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Ancient text not independently collated; not an externally verified Galen quotation.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The discussion distinguishes crisis as an alteration of the disease from an altogether local bodily motion.
preconditions: Reading the adjacent attributed definitions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Maintain difference between changed condition and change of bodily location.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The crisis supplies a judgment of the disease's turn, toward good or evil.
preconditions: A source-recognized crisis event.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The word judgment is source doctrine, not evidence of actual clinical forecast.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Lilly attributes to Hippocrates a crisis defined as 'an acute or swift reportation' of disease toward recovery or death.
preconditions: The acute or swift quality modifies the crisis/change, not a separately defined acute-illness subtype.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is Lilly's report of Hippocrates; no independent primary-source collation.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: An objection introduced 'But, say some' claims more diseases terminate in health than in death (except pestilential diseases), that in malignant/poisonous cases nature 'many times' does not fight illness, and that Hippocrates' definition would hold only in diseases ending in recovery.
preconditions: The objection is attributed to unnamed 'some', not to Hippocrates himself or Lilly's unqualified endorsement.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep the pestilential exception, comparative premise, and 'many times' rather than claiming all malignant cases lack struggle; not an empirical clinical finding.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Lilly says Avicenna in Canticis agrees with Galen, then gives Avicenna's own definition: 'est velox motus morbi ad salutem vel ad mortem' (the disease's swift movement toward health or death).
preconditions: The Latin is attributed to Avicenna by Lilly; the reported agreement with Galen does not ascribe the full Latin definition to Galen.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No independent Avicenna/Galen collation; 'motus morbi' is the movement OF disease.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Some unnamed thinkers contend that a crisis in disease arises from 'inferiour causes' and not celestial influence; the argument then considers how fever-dependent critical days might vary.
preconditions: The word 'some' refers to proponents of a general alternative theory, not only some crisis events.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The two causal accounts remain contested and historically reported, not modern scientific findings.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The argument names tertian, quartan and continued fevers as classes which would allegedly need different critical-day reckoning under the inferior-causes hypothesis.
preconditions: The proposed different calculation is conditional on the rival theory.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The denial 'cannot be' is attributed to 'many learned' rather than independently demonstrated by Lilly.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The text presents as 'more generally received and concluded' a doctrine that the Moon influences lower bodies, stirs humours and indicates disease crises by its motion.
preconditions: An historical received opinion as Lilly reports it, not an independently verified or uncontested explanation.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No empirical causal confirmation; not a medical decision rule.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The Moon's place in the zodiac at the alleged first moment of illness becomes the radix; subsequent separations and returns are followed.
preconditions: Requires timing of first sickness and Moon position.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Distinguish cyclic longitude from an actual elapsed-day count or a person's natal chart.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Where onset is unavailable, the Moon is taken at a corrected position for the first hour the patient requests advice.
preconditions: Unknown onset, alternative event time adequately specified.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The original earlier hierarchy specifies urine presentation first, then first conversation if no urine; do not erase it.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The printed table is entered using the Moon's sign and degree to locate indicative and crisis positions.
preconditions: A source-frozen lunar radix.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Table returns angular zodiac positions, not actual Gregorian calendar dates or a planetary ephemeris.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The author differentiates indicative times, semiquadrate/half crisis, a true quartile, and opposition/full crisis.
preconditions: Progression by lunar distance from radix.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not count each phase as an independent patient outcome or turn the symbolic support into probability.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The author supposes that the Moon's degree in the 'later Figure of the 16th of July 1645' was an illness-onset radix, solely to illustrate the table.
preconditions: The page says 'later Figure'; the supposed onset is not verified and not an additional patient chart.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Printed date is not a modernized civil/time-zone conversion; hypothetical illustration only.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The chapter states the Moon's place as 15 degrees 42 minutes Virgo and enters the table at 16 degrees Virgo.
preconditions: 15°42′ is the printed prose value; the approximation occurs ONLY in rounding upward to the 16-degree eighth-column table entry.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Rounding adds 18 arcminutes; do not insert 'approximately' into the original 15°42′ statement.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: For the rounded Virgo 16° radix, the first indicative entry is Libra 8°30′, where the physician might see how the disease 'would shew it selfe'.
preconditions: Source instructs entering at 16° Virgo in the eighth table column.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The 22°30′ advance is an angular illustration, not a dated medical observation.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: At an indicative or crisis point, Lilly says a favourable lunar configuration with a benevolent planet suggests 'some remisnesse' of illness; malevolent configurations suggest a bad indication.
preconditions: Evaluate the Moon's configuration to a specified planet at that event.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The phrase some remission is a hedge, not an assured recovery; no validated clinical outcome.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The next illustrative position is 1° Scorpio, at which Moon is semi-quadrate to its initial position and is 'as it were' half a crisis.
preconditions: Follow the source's row from Libra 8°30′ and a 45° angular difference.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The author explicitly hedges 'as it were'; this is not full crisis or a documented patient change.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The second indicative example is Scorpio 23 degrees 30 minutes, for judging further increase or decrease.
preconditions: Same source radix and table row.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not a second separately authenticated patient event.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The source identifies 16° Sagittarius as a true quadrature crisis, at which disease may be 'more fully discerned in one kind or other'.
preconditions: Based on hypothetical onset and rounded 16° Virgo radix, with subsequent lunar aspects separately evaluated.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Ninety degrees is symbolic geometry, not clinical validation.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The better or worse nature of the crisis at the quadrature is conditioned on aspects then formed between the Moon and other planets.
preconditions: At the source-designated quartile.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: A quadrature is not intrinsically a good or bad patient outcome without separate aspect evaluation.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Lilly instructs repeating the table lookup through the zodiac to see further indicative and crisis positions.
preconditions: Same radical Moon zodiac point.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The continued row should not be truncated at first quarter or opposition.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Alongside lunar angles, observe Moon transits over the sixth, seventh and eighth house cusps, and benefic/malefic aspects there.
preconditions: Requires a separately defined sickness question chart and reliable house cusp longitudes.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not infer natal houses or calculate a chart from the table alone.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Printed page 294 contains a 30-row multi-column critical-day longitude table with changing zodiac headings and the source caption The Table followeth.
preconditions: Use the actual page image as the primary table witness.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: ALTO linear text scrambles columns; do not treat extracted OCR order as a diplomatic table.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: A separate editorial 30×16 mathematical grid reconstructs general 22°30′ successive-column positions, but original PDF328 contains 60 systematic +1° printed departures at rows16–30 of columns3/7/11/15 plus four isolated printed anomalies.
preconditions: Printed source table/image controls; author selects 16° Virgo in its eighth column, not the nearest cell across all columns.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: 480 generated positions are NOT diplomatically transcribed/verified original cells; some damaged entries and the reason for the offset remain unresolved.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Especially at the first quartile, Lilly calls the Moon's favourable connection to a fortunate planet 'very probable' to help nature, expressly '(if the party be ordained for life)'.
preconditions: A critical day (particularly first quartile), benefic aspect/body and the author's survival qualification.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Probabilistic and survival-conditioned historical wording, not guaranteed cure or empirical prediction.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The author calls a fortunate critical-day aspect 'a good indication' and predicts a physician may restore the patient through easy medicines.
preconditions: Conditioned on the favourable aspect and 'if the party be ordained for life' caveat.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical therapeutic claim and prognosis, not proof the aspect causes recovery or safe modern advice.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: At an unlucky infortune aspect on a critical day, Lilly says the physician has 'little hopes at present', 'the Crysis is then ill', and should be more wary.
preconditions: Requires an infortune's unlucky aspect at the alleged critical moment.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep at-present time restriction; not a retrospectively verified death prediction.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The source says 'formerly men' counted days seven, fourteen and twenty-one as critical.
preconditions: This is former practice; no specific previous authorities are identified by name in this sentence.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Lilly immediately notes variable lunar motion so fixed dates cannot be used unconditionally.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Lilly says the Moon's varying motion prevents precisely fixing days seven, fourteen and twenty-one without calculating true lunar movement, directions for which he says he supplied in his 'Introduction'.
preconditions: Actual lunar motion is needed for elapsed-day timing beyond the longitude table.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No modern ephemeris parity or precise resulting timestamps in this packet.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Moon in Aries, Leo or Sagittarius is said to strengthen the attractive virtue in phlegmatic persons.
preconditions: Historical giving-medicines sign/temperament mapping.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Early-modern medical doctrine only, not recommended treatment.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Moon in Taurus, Virgo or Capricorn is said to strengthen the retentive virtue in sanguine persons.
preconditions: Moon in an earth sign, historical sanguine category.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not turn historical temperament into a validated diagnosis.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Moon in Gemini, Libra or Aquarius is said to strengthen digestive virtue in melancholic persons.
preconditions: Moon in an air sign, historical melancholic category.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not a substantiated digestive treatment mechanism.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Moon in Cancer, Scorpio or Pisces is said to strengthen expulsive virtue in choleric persons.
preconditions: Moon in a water sign, historical choleric category.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not a safe basis for purgative decisions.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Under the Moon-in-water-sign condition, a sextile or trine with Jupiter is presented for purging melancholy.
preconditions: Moon in Cancer/Scorpio/Pisces AND sextile/trine to Jupiter.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical source claim, not advice to purge or a tested treatment.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Under the Moon-in-water-sign condition, a sextile or trine with Venus is presented for purging choler.
preconditions: Moon in Cancer/Scorpio/Pisces AND sextile/trine to Venus.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not omit the shared sign/aspect restriction when representing the printed brace layout.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: When the Moon is in Cancer, Scorpio or Pisces, and in the printed sextile/trine configuration, the third historical purging row shows juxtaposed Mars (♂) and Sun (☉) glyphs next to 'Purge Phlegme'.
preconditions: Moon in a water sign plus printed sextile/trine condition; whether Mars or Sun or both is required is unresolved.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Retain both original glyphs; do NOT silently impose an 'and' or 'or' operator. Historical claim only; not care guidance.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Lilly says the retentive virtue is 'stirred up' by Saturn (♄) due to its 'frigidity' (coldness).
preconditions: Part of early-modern planet/faculty explanations.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Separate the coldness rationale from the later six-item correspondence table; not a measured mechanism.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Jupiter is associated in the printed list with vegetative and digestive virtues.
preconditions: Within the source's planetary faculty table.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical conceptual mapping, not physiological mechanism.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Mars is associated with attractive and irascible virtues.
preconditions: Within the same faculty list.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Irascible is a historical faculty label, not a modern trait diagnosis.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Sun is associated with vital and natural potency.
preconditions: Within the same faculty list.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: One source category, not two independent patient observations.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Venus is associated with appetitive and concupiscible virtues.
preconditions: Within the same faculty list.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not infer modern hormones or sexual behaviour.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Mercury is associated with cogitative and imaginative virtues.
preconditions: Within the same faculty list.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: An attributed historical schema, not neurocognitive validation.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Moon is associated with the expulsive virtue.
preconditions: Within the same faculty list.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is separate from Moon's sign-based temperament classification.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: The text links fiery signs Aries, Leo and Sagittarius to red choler.
preconditions: Historical four-element humour scheme.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not replace red choler with modern inflammatory disease.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Earth signs Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn are linked to black melancholy; an original erratum additionally directs reading the Latin adjective as atram.
preconditions: Printed earth/melancholy correspondence with same-volume errata.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Erratum target line and body typography remain separately collated; no classical source validation.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Air signs Gemini, Libra and Aquarius are linked to blood.
preconditions: Historical humoral classification.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not infer modern hematology or blood testing.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Water signs Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces are linked to spittle and phlegm.
preconditions: Historical humoral classification.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not actual mucus measurement or treatment validation.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Lilly says he had intended a larger discussion of sickness but refrains because Master Booker promised the work.
preconditions: Editorial boundary at the end of the chapter.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not invent missing source rules from the promised unwritten discourse.

source_locator.source_original: William Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Wellcome b30338724

rules.source_statement: Chapter XLVII ends before the divider on PDF330; Chapter XLVIII begins below it, asking whether a servant shall be freed from his master.
preconditions: Text on PDF330 above and below the separator.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Next chapter's servant/master mechanics must not enter this illness/crisis packet.
